question: _________________ recommend(s) 20 mm wide margins for sheet sizes AO and A1 in engineering drawings.
solution:
__**Explanation:**__

SP: 46 (2003) refers to the Indian Standard Code of Practice for Engineering Drawing. It serves as a guideline for creating standardized engineering drawings that meet specific dimensions, tolerances, and presentation criteria. Among its stipulations, SP: 46 (2003) recommends maintaining 20 mm wide margins for sheet sizes AO and A1 in engineering drawings to ensure clarity, uniformity, and proper presentation.

**Purpose of Borders and Frames**

 
• **Enhancing Visual Organization:** Borders and frames help in organizing the content of the drawing. They define the limits of the drawing area and provide a clear boundary for the information presented.
 
• **Improving Clarity:** With appropriate margins and borders, the drawing becomes easier to read and interpret, especially in collaborative environments where multiple stakeholders review the documents.
 
• **Facilitating Reproduction:** Standardized margins ensure that the drawing remains intact and legible when reproduced, whether through printing or scanning.
 
• **Compliance with Standards:** Adhering to SP: 46 (2003) ensures that the engineering drawings meet national and international standards, promoting consistency and reliability in documentation.

**Correct Option Analysis:**

The correct option is:

**Option 1:** Borders and Frames: SP: 46 (2003)

This option correctly identifies the source of the guideline recommending 20 mm wide margins for sheet sizes AO and A1 in engineering drawings. SP: 46 (2003) serves as the authoritative standard for such specifications, ensuring uniformity and compliance in engineering documentation
